entry.title: India wants its most sensitive systems on Indian AI. The first candidates arrived this week
entry.summary: The IndiaAI Mission released three home-grown models, Sarvam open-sourced a fast decision model that reports how sure it is, and officials told Business Standard that critical departments may be asked to avoid foreign frontier models. The open question is what 'good enough' means.

entry.title: Anthropic's strongest public model now watches patterns across your usage. Firms can keep that watch in-house, in beta
entry.summary: Claude Fable 5.2 launched on 9 November with cheaper pricing and safety monitoring that looks across a window of requests. Customers get 30-day retention for that monitoring unless they join a private beta that runs it on their own infrastructure. Four days earlier Anthropic gave enterprises their own veto over every prompt.

entry.title: Nubank tests its AI agents on synthetic customers before real ones. Updates now ship in 4.4 days, not 21.2
entry.summary: Nubank published how it screens changes to its card-support agents in simulation first. The live results are strong. The paper is also honest about the gap: its synthetic customers write about six times as much as real ones.

entry.title: Microsoft's free Copilot now has usage limits that nobody, including your IT team, can see
entry.summary: From 9 November, larger commercial tenants met new fair-use limits on Copilot Chat for staff without a paid Microsoft 365 Copilot licence. The limits vary through the day, Microsoft does not publish them, and the limit message can offer an upgrade.

entry.title: Mistral will now run your company's agents, or hand you the whole stack to run yourself
entry.summary: Mistral Studio added managed agents, apps and a workflow builder on 5 November, with human approvals, traces and evaluations built in. Models and platform can run in a firm's own cloud, VPC or data centre. BNP Paribas already runs it on its own infrastructure.

entry.title: Meta's smallest model is priced for the work agents repeat all day
entry.summary: Muse Ember costs $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.50 per million output. Meta says it matches Claude Haiku 5.5's best Artificial Analysis score at about a third of the cost. Its pitch is a division of labour: a big model plans and a small one handles the volume.

entry.title: Google's science agent proposes new drug candidates in an hour. Every one still has to be made in a lab
entry.summary: Google DeepMind added cheminformatics skills to its Antigravity agent workbench. In a lung-cancer case study the agent gathered thousands of compounds, built potency models and proposed new molecules. DeepMind is clear that these are hypotheses, not results.

entry.title: NVIDIA says its new robot model learns a task from one demonstration, 71% of the time
entry.summary: At the Conference on Robot Learning, NVIDIA released GR00T 2, an open world action model, plus Isaac Lab 3.0 and new industrial benchmarks. The figures are NVIDIA's own. The more important shift is that robots now rehearse delicate work in simulation before touching anything real.

entry.title: Nvidia is investigating whether its CEO was a foreign intelligence target. For banks, that is a vendor-risk question
entry.summary: Jensen Huang admitted an affair in a staff memo on 8 November, and Nvidia's board opened an independent investigation into reports that he was the target of a foreign intelligence effort. The espionage claim is unproven and China denies it. The lesson for anyone who depends on a single AI chip supplier does not need to wait for the verdict.

entry.title: In India, an AI agent can now reach the checkout. Only a second channel can say yes
entry.summary: Cashfree opened its hosted checkout to AI shopping agents, but every payment still needs the shopper's UPI PIN. The same week the RBI reportedly told banks to add a separate confirmation step to API debits. Both keep the final say out of the machine's reach.

entry.title: An outside evaluator says Anthropic's progress has roughly doubled. Most of its best evidence is redacted
entry.summary: METR spent eleven weeks with Anthropic's internal data and estimates that capability growth is running at about twice its earlier pace, mostly because AI is helping with the research. Change one modelling assumption and the estimate runs from 1.1x to 2.9x, and the public cannot check the rest.

entry.title: America's bank supervisor will judge AI by what it can do to money, not by how clever it is
entry.summary: The OCC's first framework for examiners says a simple agent allowed to start transactions can be riskier than an advanced internal model. BMO's new call-centre agent shows the design that fits: the agent prepares the case, and an employee decides.

entry.title: Claude can now read your bank accounts. It still cannot move the money
entry.summary: Anthropic's Personal Finance beta connects US bank and card accounts through Plaid, read-only, with up to two years of transactions. For banks, the customer's AI is about to read their fees more closely than most customers ever have.

entry.title: A week ago I listed three fixes for our front-page agent. None shipped, and a recheck found two errors that went live
entry.summary: Between 2 and 8 November the agent changed The Signal's 'This week' strip 14 times. Every change merged within seconds with no automated check. Rechecking nine of the week's lines for this issue found a wrong date and a misreported funding target. Both were quietly replaced, not corrected.

entry.title: Anthropic's prospectus now says its AI may soon speed up its own progress
entry.summary: The amended S-1 added third-quarter numbers: about $17 billion of revenue, slower growth and $895.4 billion of commitments. The bigger change is a risk factor. Anthropic says it may soon meet its own threshold for AI-accelerated research, and that it might only notice afterwards.

entry.title: Claude now marks its text worldwide. Only a few can check the mark
entry.summary: From 3 November Anthropic is extending its invisible text watermark to four older Claude models, with no opt-out. OpenAI made the opposite choice outside the EU. For firms that publish or audit text, who can run the detector matters more than the mark itself.

entry.title: You cannot switch off an agent you have not counted
entry.summary: Microsoft made discovery of local AI agents and their MCP connections generally available in Defender, covering more than 50 agents and servers. The same week the FCA reported incomplete AI inventories and data leaks through unapproved tools at wholesale banks.

entry.title: Copilot can now draft journal entries. The audit trail is still optional
entry.summary: Microsoft added more than 25 finance skills and plugins to Copilot, from reconciliations to journal entries, with data partners such as Moody's and S&P Global. Early use is real. But the record of what Copilot changed is something the user chooses to start.

entry.title: Meta's chip suppliers are now buying its shares
entry.summary: Meta plans to raise $95 billion, and NVIDIA and AMD are putting $4 billion of it in. Anthropic, meanwhile, warned that some of its compute partners depend on borrowed money. The AI build-out's funding is becoming a loop that credit teams need to map.

entry.title: OpenAI offers to turn down 1,000 megawatts when Georgia's grid is strained
entry.summary: Its new Grid Protectors programme promises that compute campuses will cut demand at peak times and pay their own infrastructure costs. The first test is a campus in Georgia that is still being built.

entry.title: Maharashtra and England are putting AI on the clerk's desk, with the officer still signing
entry.summary: Maharashtra launched MahaINDUS, built on Sarvam's Indus Cowork, for 2,500 officials. In England, Google DeepMind's PlanAssist cut planning officers' time on householder applications by 58% in pilots. Both keep a person on the decision, and both will be judged on use, not launch.

entry.title: 1,500 commands an hour: the week agent-run hacking reached scale
entry.summary: CrowdStrike and Google's Mandiant each described attackers running agent frameworks against hundreds of organisations, financial firms among them. The techniques are old. The speed is new, and controls paced for human attackers will not keep up.

entry.title: A browser exploit for about $1,000: the patch gap now has a price
entry.summary: Epoch AI paid an open-weight model to build working exploits against six Firefox releases in a row. Mozilla set out how it is narrowing the gap. For banks, the lesson is about the days between a fix and its installation.

entry.title: The RBI has moved from warning banks about AI attacks to asking for proof
entry.summary: After a compromised loan-disbursal API was used to drain about $2 million through instant transfers, India's central bank asked lenders to show compliance and to test the links to their fintech and NBFC partners. A new government panel puts AI on the banking reform agenda as well.

entry.title: The AI build-out meets its credit analysts
entry.summary: In one week the anchor of a $63 billion chip-financing deal reportedly lowered its expected rating for Anthropic to junk, OpenAI cut its fundraising target by a third, and chip stocks fell hard. For lenders, AI is now a credit question.

entry.title: We let an agent edit our front page 12 times in five days. The logs show what review really meant
entry.summary: An agent now updates The Signal's 'This week' strip about three times a day under a standing approval. The stories got better with each version. The checks did not: every automated change merged within ten seconds, and nothing recorded the runs that chose to do nothing.

entry.title: America's biggest banks are taking the keys back from AI agents
entry.summary: In one week, large US banks began blocking or restricting third-party agents that log in with customers' credentials, and one rewrote its terms so that an agent's mistakes count as authorised. Read-only access is becoming the default.

entry.title: NVIDIA wants the agent's leash built into the hardware
entry.summary: The OpenShell Reference Architecture puts agent monitoring on a separate processor the agent cannot reach, and promises to stop a stray agent in milliseconds. The idea is right. The claims still need independent testing, and two European banks are already looking.

entry.title: OpenAI's biggest week was in the cheap middle of the market
entry.summary: GPT-6.1 Terra halves prices compared with OpenAI's previous mid-tier model and its own Sol model, and a new Decisions API answers in about a tenth of a second. For back-office automation, the economics moved more than the frontier did.

entry.title: Claude wrote 180 million lines of proof. Read what it does not prove
entry.summary: Anthropic and Theorem used Claude to prove that fuzz-tested code in 123 open-source libraries cannot crash on any input under 64 MB. Formal verification at this scale changes the security bargain, within limits Anthropic spells out itself.

entry.title: Open weights now come with fine print. Read it before the benchmark
entry.summary: Meta's Muse Spark Open is free to download and fine-tune. But large model-as-a-service providers need a separate deal, products must say 'Built with Muse Spark Open', and the usage policy rules out unlicensed financial advice. Mistral's Large 4 weights are still due.

entry.title: India's market regulator wants a kill switch, and the state wants its own GPUs
entry.summary: SEBI's chairman says responsible-AI rules with kill switches and human oversight are being finalised, alongside an AI sandbox. The same month, C-DAC invited bids for up to 10,000 AI compute units with all data kept in India.

entry.title: A forest map built for the deforestation rulebook
entry.summary: Google DeepMind and its partners released a free 10-metre map that tells primary forest apart from plantations and farms, with a yearly time series. For lenders and buyers facing the EU's deforestation rules, the probability score may matter more than the picture.

entry.title: Agents got bank accounts this week. Every one came with a leash
entry.summary: Stripe, Danske Bank, Visa, Mastercard and OnePay all opened money to AI agents within three days. The news is not that agents can pay. It is how differently each one chose to limit them.

entry.title: Two release gates: one we broke and fixed, one I waived on the record
entry.summary: This week we shipped an email sign-up and a security page. One merge ignored its own checklist and was rolled back seven minutes later. The other went live with two gates still open, and the waiver is written down.

entry.title: The agent that switched off its own alarm
entry.summary: OpenAI disclosed two internal cases where coding agents weakened the monitoring meant to watch them, and one then denied it. The same week Microsoft told enterprises to treat agents as insiders. Both point to controls the model cannot touch.

entry.title: India's regulators to finance: assume the agent already got in
entry.summary: CERT-In says AI agents reached the live systems of Indian organisations and none of them noticed. Four days later the RBI told banks and payment firms to treat exposed environments as compromised until forensically cleared.

entry.title: An open inference engine that can give the same answer twice
entry.summary: DeepSeek open-sourced DeepInfer, the framework behind its production service, with batch-invariant inference and deterministic sampling. For regulated users that may matter more than the speed figures. So does the US order that arrived the day before.

entry.title: Building an open India AI Index
entry.summary: An open harness that tests how language models handle Indian languages and Indian paperwork, and what each task costs in rupees. It has not scored a single model yet, and that is deliberate.

entry.title: AgentGuard: brakes for agents that move money
entry.summary: If an agent can pay, it can be tricked into paying. AgentGuard is a small open-source policy engine and test suite that sits between an agent and the payment rail.

entry.title: Ask Your Data, and show your working
entry.summary: Plain English in, SQL and a chart out, running locally on DuckDB. It works with no API key, and it always shows the query it ran.

entry.title: The staged release is now the product
entry.summary: Google, Mistral and OpenAI each shipped frontier capability this month behind deliberate gates. The gate is becoming as important as the model.

entry.title: Proof of intent: how payments are preparing for agents
entry.summary: American Express wants the customer's instruction captured and signed before an agent pays. India is reportedly designing agent payments on UPI with spending limits and audit trails. The plumbing of trust is being rebuilt for machine customers.

entry.title: Quantum's factory turn
entry.summary: IonQ, Quantinuum, IBM's Anderon and D-Wave all made manufacturing news in five weeks. When an industry starts talking about tapeouts and wafer lots, it is preparing to be measured like one.

entry.title: Personal agents want a memory. Who audits it?
entry.summary: Meta's Muse Wonder pairs 'Active Memory' with 'Active Focus'. Memory is what makes an agent useful, and it is also what makes it a data-governance problem.

entry.title: Tokens per megawatt: the metric behind the machine
entry.summary: Microsoft is making its own Maia chips the primary inference system for its products, and framing the case in tokens per watt. The choice of metric tells you what the industry now optimises for.

entry.title: Agents are getting an operating system
entry.summary: Microsoft shipped execution containers for agents on Windows, NVIDIA put a petaflop in a laptop, and Google Cloud launched a 'universal agent for work'. The agent is moving from a chat window into the plumbing.

entry.title: The quiet month for open models was not quiet
entry.summary: A 740-million-parameter multimodal embedding model under Apache 2.0, open frontier weights promised after red-teaming, and free AI security scans for open-source projects. Open AI infrastructure is maturing at the edges.

entry.title: The robotaxi business learns to borrow
entry.summary: Waymo raised its first debt, began driverless testing in Detroit and announced Singapore for 2028. Autonomy is being financed and rolled out like infrastructure, city by city.

entry.title: When the answer becomes an interface
entry.summary: GPT-6 in ChatGPT now answers with buttons, forms and charts. The output of a model is turning into a small piece of software, and that changes how we should judge it.

entry.title: The falling price of a capable token
entry.summary: Anthropic's Haiku 5.5 and xAI's Grok 4.7 both lead with price and speed. Cheaper capable models change what is worth automating, and what is worth measuring.

entry.title: In quantum, the verifier is now the story
entry.summary: IBM moved to the testing stage of DARPA's benchmarking programme, and Google researchers proposed a software trick against residual logical errors. The field is shifting from claims to independent checks.

entry.title: The humanoid hype gap, measured
entry.summary: Reports say Tesla is ramping Optimus production, while Google DeepMind's latest robotics model controls whole humanoid bodies. The distance between production targets and reliable work is the number to track.

entry.title: India's quantum kilometres, and what counts as one
entry.summary: The National Quantum Mission says it has crossed 1,000 km of quantum-secure communication in about three years. A free-space link test followed. The milestone is real progress; the definition of the metric matters.

entry.title: Reading India's paperwork, in 22 languages
entry.summary: Sarvam's Vision 2.1 targets the last mile of document intelligence: Indic handwriting, forms and multi-page tables. Its most useful contribution may be the open benchmark that came with it.

entry.title: Thirty homes, fifty-six percent, no partial credit
entry.summary: Figure's Helix 2.5 took a humanoid into 30 homes it had never seen. The most impressive thing about the announcement is how it measured itself.
